To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose an online generative discriminative Restricted Boltzman machine (OGD RBMs) that provides the flexibility to grow the network architecture according to the statistics on the fly and we demonstrate that the online RBMs outperform batch RBMs in terms of accuracy and the number of hidden neurons required to achieve the accuracy.

OGD RBMs can learn to adapt to non stationary data streams in a single pass, unsupervised manner and can be trained in a single pass to be discriminatively trained to the class labels in an online manner.
OGD RBMs provide an online learning approach for training RBMs in a single pass and that the online generatively learned RBM features provide better discriminative power than batch learned features.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an online learning algorithm that provides the ability of growing RBM on the data stream and adapting the network architecture of the model according to the statistics and the class distribution of the incoming data.
developing a novel online learning approach for training RBM that is capable of learning the network architecture from data.
the design of an online deep learning architecture, the OGD RBMs, that can be applied for non stationary data mining problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we propose a novel online generative discriminative Restricted Boltzman Machine that provides the ability for building and adapting the network architecture of an RBM to statistics of streaming non stationary data.
the OGD RBMs are a new class of RBMs, which are able to learn and adapt their network architecture to the data on the fly in an unsupervised manner.
the OGD RBMs are able to provide a good feature representation and classification for the streaming data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an online learning algorithm for RBM that is capable of building the RBM architecture on the fly and adapting to the statistics of the streaming data.
we have proposed a novel online generative discriminative Restricted Boltzman Machine that can be applied for classification problems in data mining applications.
the online generatively trained RBM is a powerful and scalable tool for unsupervised learning, and that it provides the flexibility to adapt to non stationary data streams.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a generative model can be trained online in an adaptive manner to learn a concise feature representation that can be used for discriminative tasks.

online generative training is a powerful unsupervised learning approach for feature representation that can be used in conjunction with discriminative training to achieve state of the art performance in non stationary data streams.
the network structure can be adapted online to the statistics of the data.
